# Test Writing Guide

## Framework

- Bun Test (`bun:test`) — `describe`, `test`, `expect`, `beforeEach`
- Run all tests: `bun test`
- Run one file: `bun test <file>`
- Run `bun test` only from a directory whose `bunfig.toml` loads the host-safety preload guard: the repository root, `tests/` or `tests/integration/`. Bun reads only the `bunfig.toml` in the directory `bun test` starts in (it does not search upward). The repository root and every directory holding a test file have one whose first `[test]` `preload` entry names the guard, which loads before any test file and any other preload (see Host safety under Isolation). Started in a directory with no `bunfig.toml` (outside the repository, or one holding no test file, such as `src/`), the run has no guard. Start every run with its own scratch HOME, outside your home directory, and `SLACK_STATE_DIR` under it, as `tests/README.md` shows: the guard refuses to start (exit 78) when the home the run was launched with could reach the operator's real state (see The launch-home refusal under Host safety)
- When stdout is not a TTY (piped, or run by an agent), Bun prints only failing test titles. To see the passing titles, such as a `test.each` matrix's rows, run it in a TTY or add `--reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=<path>`

## Test File Organization

Each source module has a corresponding test file under `tests/`. Every `tests/*.test.ts` file appears in exactly one row below; a new test file gets a row, and a deleted one loses it:

| Source | Test File | What It Tests |
|--------|-----------|---------------|
| lib.ts, liveness-reading.ts (a `pending` row's launch start), server.ts (`_buildIsSessionAliveAdapter` and its liveness readings (C12), `_buildReconnectSessionAdapter` (with its latched gate, b.jg5 SRJ-502, its `working`-row verdict and `waiting`-row check, one `read-pane` each, b.jg5 SRJ-603, SRJ-604, and its prompt-row verdict, one one-line `read-pane`, b.jg5 SRJ-606), `_buildKillSessionAdapter`, `deferPendingRow`, `_runCallTimeoutStartStep`, UNAVAILABLE and read errors at call sites (b.jg5 SRJ-105), UNCLASSIFIED at call sites (b.jg5 SRJ-313), UNUSABLE NAME at the adapters' `status` (b.jg5 SRJ-512), a `pending` row with no launch start at the adapters' `status` (b.jg5 SRJ-513)) | server.test.ts | assertSendable (state-dir rule, with its path boundaries: an `inbox`-prefixed sibling such as `inbox-old`, a sibling named after the state dir such as `<state>2`, a trailing separator; the same rule on real paths through symlinks in a `mkdtempSync` dir, a state dir given through a symlink included; also refuses each listed credentials file by real path, symlinks included), chunkText, sanitizeFilename. A `pending` row's launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-115), through the pure readers: a `pending` `status` result showing a launch start, with or without fractional seconds, has it read raw (`pendingLaunchStartOf`), and `livenessReadingForStatus` gives a frozen `pending` reading carrying it, equal to `pendingLivenessReading(start)`, from which `launchStartOfReading` gives it back; a launch start that is absent, `null`, empty, not a string or behind a throwing getter gives none and the plain `pending` reading, with no throw; another state's launch start is ignored (each state reads as it would with none); no result, or one whose state cannot be read, gives no launch start and reads `unknown`; `pendingLivenessReading` with no or an empty launch start gives the plain reading; and `launchStartOfReading` gives none for a `pending` reading without a non-empty string launch start, for any other reading and for anything that is not a reading. The `dead` reading's install-gone source (b.jg5 SRJ-610, SRJ-1016; describe "liveness-reading: the dead reading's install-gone source"): `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE` is frozen and of the same kind as `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD` (`livenessKindOf`) yet not equal to it, and `isInstallGoneDeadReading` holds for it alone: false for every other reading (a row read's `dead` included), for a reading of another kind carrying its source, for a `dead` reading with another source, for a reading whose `source` getter throws (with no throw) and for a value that is not a reading. The session-alive adapter over the agent-director stub, with a trigger-sink spy and a cleared-flag observer spy installed, answers a liveness reading (b.jg5 SRJ-314): each state `status` answers maps to its reading, and with both flags raised clears `ad-unreachable` only (the observer told of that class alone) while `tmux-unavailable` stays raised with no all-clear, since a `status` is not tmux-touching (b.jg5 SRJ-312, AC 27, AC 36; every live state but `pending` reads `live`, `pending` reads `pending`, `ended` and `missing` read `dead`, a state CSCB does not know reads `unknown`); with `ad-unreachable` raised alone, a live state clears it with its one all-clear; with one unknown-state line naming the persona for a state CSCB does not know and none for a known state; a `pending` result showing a launch start reads `pending` carrying it raw (b.jg5 SRJ-115), one showing none under a key no configured persona uses (the configured-persona query counting no key, b.jg5 SRJ-408) reads the plain `pending` reading with no `launchStartedAt`, and a `live` result carrying a launch start reads `live` with none (one case each here; the permutations are the pure readers' above); `ErrSpawnNotFound` reads `dead` and, with both flags raised, clears `ad-unreachable` only, leaving `tmux-unavailable` raised with no all-clear and nothing armed (b.jg5 SRJ-312), while with `ad-unreachable` raised alone it clears it with its one all-clear; `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` sets `ad-unreachable` with the binary path and reads `dead` from the install-gone source (`LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE`, `isInstallGoneDeadReading` true), while every other `dead` reading the adapter gives (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, an unknown key) carries no such source; `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` sets `tmux-unavailable`, reads `unknown`, not dead, and reports the ENVIRONMENT cause once for the persona outside any attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-311); the adapter is a raise site of its own, so the form it is handed picks the onset (b.jg5 SRJ-1021): the re-bound-socket form (`errTmuxNotAvailableDifferentServer`) posts `tmuxServerChangedOnset()` and plain `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` the `tmux-unavailable` template's onset (the two texts checked to differ), each posted once with the ENVIRONMENT cause armed once, reading `unknown` and nothing leaked; and in either order, a second probe answering the other form while the flag is raised reads `unknown` and posts nothing, the first form's onset the only one; a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316), outside any attempt and inside a recovery attempt for the persona, reads `unknown`, not dead, raises `ad-config-malformed` and posts `adConfigMalformedOnset(err)` once, its description (a fake token in a `ticket=` URL) redacted and then escaped (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`), reports the CONFIG cause once per probe, and logs one raise line beside the `status error` line, a second probe adding only its `status error` line; with `ad-config-malformed` raised, a successful `status` (read `live`) or `ErrSpawnNotFound` (read `dead`) clears it with one clear line and one all-clear listing the bare class, or with no all-clear when `tmux-unavailable` is also raised, which stays (b.jg5 SRJ-312), while `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, the UNAVAILABLE forms and `ErrInternal` leave it raised with no clear line or all-clear, each keeping its own reading, and post exactly the onset of a class the error itself raises (`ad-unreachable` with the binary path for `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, `tmux-unavailable` for `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) or nothing; every other `status` error (`ErrCallTimeout`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrInternal`, a wrapped UnknownError, a name from a later binary, a plain `Error`, another STATE name, an UNUSABLE name, `ErrSchemaMismatch`, a GONE name) reads `unknown`, not dead, with no flag, nothing posted, one log line and, outside any attempt, nothing armed; with an unclassified-sink spy installed too (b.jg5 SRJ-313: reads count toward the episode), a `status` answering `ErrInternal`, `ErrSchemaMismatch` or a name CSCB gives no handling inside a restart run for the persona reads `unknown`, arms the read-error cause once and is reported once to the unclassified sink, inside the attempt, as the value itself, with one token-safe `status error` line, while `ErrInternal` outside any attempt or inside a restart run for another persona reports and arms nothing; `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, inside a restart run for the persona or outside one, reads `dead` from the install-gone source, raises `ad-unreachable` and is never reported to the unclassified sink (inside the run it arms the read-error cause, outside nothing); each persona is probed as `cscb_<key>`; an unknown key, or no persona config, reads `dead` with no status call. The reconnect adapter (b.9a7), its harness (`makeHarness`) scripting each attempt's pane reads (`paneQueue`, then `paneError`, then `pane`, the last two read at each read); its file-local helpers are `fullPaneReads(n)` (`n` reads of `cscb_C1` with `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES`), `probePaneReads(n)` (`n` one-line reads of `cscb_C1` with `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES`), `escalateDeadLine(verdict)` (the sweep line from the imported `escalateDeadSweepLine`, carrying its evidence text from `ESCALATE_DEAD_EVIDENCE`), `paneGone()` (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed` for C1's session) and `endedTranscript()` (a finished turn's transcript and the row fields naming it): a `working` row of a persona whose launch is in flight returns `transient` with no `read-pane`, reconnect typed or sweep, even with a `read-pane` that would answer GONE (bug b.d61); a `waiting` row makes one `read-pane` of its own row before `/mcp reconnect` is typed (b.jg5 SRJ-604); a `pending` row (bug b.dup) under a key no configured persona uses (b.jg5 SRJ-408) returns `pending` (b.jg5 SRJ-303), with no send-keys, pane read or sweep, no notice and one `Deferring persona=<key>: its row reads pending` line, which names the row's launch start raw when its `status` result shows one (b.jg5 SRJ-115); the query is asked right after the `status` read (before any branch on the state), right after a `working` row's `read-pane` and after a `waiting` row's `read-pane` that answered GONE or found the row absent, right after a prompt row's `read-pane`, right before each not-connected notice of the `working`, `waiting` and prompt-row checks (the unproven-idle notice a noted deferral can raise, and the blocked-on-prompt notice), and right before typing: a `waiting` row whose persona is latched returns `transient` right after its `status` read, the query asked once for the key, no pane read, nothing typed or swept, no kill, spawn or resume, and one `reconnectSession: persona=<key> is latched — not typing /mcp reconnect; Attempt frames run on the bare controller as the sink: a `test.each` over an attempt started later from inside a closed attempt (by a real 0 ms `setTimeout` callback, set inside the attempt and awaited, or by a promise continuation), with an enclosing attempt still open or none, finds the new attempt is not nested in the closed one: `isInsideAttempt` is true for its own key and the open outer key only, a report arms only those keys and is recorded in their own `lastError` (the closed attempt's stays unset), the closed key is never armed, and every closed key answers false afterwards. Again-reasons and `close` (SRJ-303, SRJ-305), on the bare controller: a `test.each` over an `again` answer's reason (a label, a token-shaped reason, a non-string) finds it named in the re-armed line only (the last two as `unnamed`) and never recorded as a cause; `close` stops every persona with one stopped line each, refuses a later arm with one `not armed` line, fires nothing more and leaves nothing pending, and a run in flight at `close` finishes with its answer dropped and nothing re-armed. The retry action (`createFullModeRetryAction`) over a stand-in row read and retry entry: in full mode, a `test.each` over all sixteen restart outcomes maps already-connected and reconnected to the nothing-left-to-recover stop (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RECOVERED`), capped, not-up, launch-skipped, shutting-down and latched to their stops (latched to `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`), and in-flight, refused (a bare `again`), counted-failure, reconnect-deferred, pending-deferred (with `row: 'pending'`), launched (with `row: 'pending'` and `switchToPendingOnly: true`), liveness-unknown (with `keepsLastRow: true`, b.jg5 SRJ-314), sequence-waiting (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_SEQUENCE_WAITING`, b.jg5 SRJ-706) and not-initialised to `again` with their reasons, each calling the entry once with the persona's working directory and reading no row. In pending-only mode, a retry that finds a launch in flight makes no row read and no entry call and answers `again` with the `launch-in-flight` reason and `row: 'pending'`, a throwing predicate counting as in flight; otherwise each retry makes one row read, inside a recovery attempt for the persona, and no entry call: `pending` answers `again` with the `row-pending` reason and `row: 'pending'`, the same for a `pending` row read carrying a launch start in each sample form (b.jg5 SRJ-115), and `waiting`, `working` and `check_permission` stop with the row-live reason, the row and `yieldsToFullMode: true`; `ended`, `missing` and `absent` stop with the row-gone reason, the row, a hand-off that, run once, calls the entry once, and `yieldsToFullMode: true`; a row read that rejects rejects the action. In both modes, before the row read or the entry runs, and in that order, shutting down, not applied, latched (`isLatched`, b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305: `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`), not up and at the restart cap each stop it with neither called; over the stand-ins in both modes, a latched query that throws stops it with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`, the not-up and cap gates, the row read and the entry never asked, with one `the latched query failed: … — taken as latched` line, redacted; the entry gets the action's own in-flight predicate (`isInFlight`, the same function the action was given; production gives it "blocks a retry", `isPersonaRetryBlocked`, never "in flight for P"), and an entry that rejects rejects the action; the latched query is asked again after the row read: in pending-only mode, a persona that latches during that read (the row answering `ended`) stops with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` after that one read, with no hand-off and no entry call. The full-mode retry end to end (SRJ-302, SRJ-303, SRJ-305) on the harness's default action, with a file-local `modelRow` answering each persona's `status` from a given state (`absent` as `ErrSpawnNotFound`) until a spawn for it resolves and `waiting` after (`set` starts that over from another state): AC 26, with both settings 0 and agent-director's default settings, a bring-up refused by `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` starts the condition at its time and spawns again at each due time and never 1 ms early, each refused retry logging its re-armed line (`retry <n>: unavailable: … — re-armed, next retry in <s> s`) with the next wait, through `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP` plus the refusals to the ceiling plus two, counting nothing and never reaching `onCapReached`; that retry then fires at its due time, past the alert check's, and no alert is ever posted, with nothing counted; a `test.each` over the row a retry finds (live and connected: stopped, one `status` call; live and not connected: a reconnect, no spawn, stopped; `pending`, not connected or connected with its stream: the liveness read defers it (b.jg5 SRJ-314), one `status` call, no reconnect and no spawn, never stopped with nothing left to recover, re-armed in full mode with the `pending-deferred` reason and its last row read `pending`; `ended` or missing: a spawn with no kill, re-armed in pending-only mode), each checking the stub's call counts, the whole view on a re-arm, the other persona still armed and no failure counted; with the harness's restart deps given the `pending` deferral as `main()` binds it (b.jg5 SRJ-314, SRJ-115), a retry that finds the row `pending` with a launch start and the session connected with its stream hands it, with its launch start, to the deferral once (one `status` call, one deferral line naming the launch start), with no kill, spawn, resume or send-keys, nothing counted, no cap and no trigger, re-arms at the next wait in full mode with the `pending-deferred` reason and its last row read `pending`, is kept through either condition end, and a following retry that finds the row live, connected and with its stream makes one `status` call and stops with nothing left to recover; a retry that finds the launch in flight (`holdSpawns`) makes no agent-director call and re-arms at the doubled wait with the `launch-in-flight` reason, and once the launch settles the next retry stops with nothing left to recover; The stop rules that exist now (SRJ-305, AC 28) on the harness: the restart cap, where each counted launch failure (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) re-arms at the doubled wait with the `launch-failed` reason until the cap stops the timer, with exactly one spawn per retry (none in a failed one's place, b.jg5 SRJ-602), one `onCapReached` and its notice, the other persona still armed; a retry queued behind restart work (a `runRestartRetry` whose held launch fails with `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` one failure short of the cap) answers capped from its entry once that failure reaches the cap: one relaunch line and one spawn in all (the held one, none in its place), the stub's calls one `status` and no kill, the count at `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`, one `onCapReached` and one cap notice, one `Restart retry skipped for persona=<key> — the persona is at the restart cap; nothing killed or launched` line in `errors`, and the timer stopped with the capped line; a `test.each` over a persona not up (`setUp`), out of the applied configuration (`remove`) or already at the cap, whose next retry stops the timer with no agent-director call while the other persona's due time is kept and its retry proceeds; a trigger for a key no longer applied arms it, and its first retry stops it with no call; `teardown` stops the persona's timer at once, which never fires, the other staying armed; `shutdown` stops every timer, a later launch refused UNAVAILABLE logs one `not armed` line and is a plain failure, not `retrying` (the closed controller's sink answers false), and nothing fires however far the clock goes. Pending-only mode (SRJ-301, SRJ-303, SRJ-305) on the harness's default action, armed directly through `controller.armPendingOnly`: a row still `pending` is armed at the base wait with one `armed in pending-only mode (pending-row)` line, cause `pending-row` and last row `pending`, and each of two retries logs its `retry <n> (pending-only) — reading its row` line, makes one `status` call for `cscb_<key>` and the pending-row step's one `get` (the row covered) and no other, and re-arms at the doubled wait with the `row-pending` reason, the other persona unarmed and nothing counted (both settings 0); a row read failing UNAVAILABLE (`ErrCallTimeout`) or GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`, `read-error`) is a trigger inside the attempt that promotes the timer to full mode, the failed retry re-arms at the next wait (`re-armed in full mode`), and the next retry runs the full decision (connected: stopped, nothing left to recover); a pending-only retry while a launch is in flight (`holdSpawns`) makes no agent-director call and re-arms at the doubled wait with the `launch-in-flight` reason, the last row read `pending`, and once the launch settles the next retry makes its one read; The pending and kill-failure exceptions (SRJ-306), the condition-end entry `conditionEnded(key, condition)` called directly on the harness with no reading: with the last row read `pending` (armed pending-only directly, or a full-mode retry deferred on the pending row), the end of `tmux-unresponsive` and of `tmux-unavailable` each answer `kept` with one `kept — <condition ended>, but its row last read pending` line, the view and due time unchanged; The switch, the last row read and a condition end during a run (SRJ-301, SRJ-306), on the bare controller with a held stand-in action: a `launched` answer takes the switch to pending-only mode with no other cause, and stays in full mode with a `kill-failed` cause recorded before the run or another arm during it, its last row read `pending` either way and the next retry run in that mode; `armPendingOnly` on a full-mode timer during a run, then an `again` with no row, leaves the last row read `pending` (a condition end keeps the timer); during a run, then an `again` with its own row, the answer's row wins (a condition end stops it); before the run, then an `again` with no row, clears the last row (a condition end stops it); before the run, then an `again` with no row that keeps the last row read (`keepsLastRow`, a liveness reading of `unknown`), leaves it `pending` (a condition end keeps the timer). A condition end during a run answers `deferred` and logs nothing, and is applied once the run has answered: stopped with the condition's reason and nothing pending after an `again` with no row and after an `again` with row `waiting`; kept, one kept line and then the re-armed line, after a `launched` answer (re-armed in pending-only mode), after a failed run with the row last read `pending` (armed pending-only) and after an `again` with a `kill-failed` cause recorded; moot, only the stopped line, after a `stop` answer and after a stop during the run (its `again` answer dropped); two ends during one run apply the latest condition once: kept after a `launched` answer, a later run applying none, and stopped with the latest condition's reason after an `again` with no row. ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`; b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-312, SRJ-305, SRJ-306, AC 27, AC 36) on `makeRecoveryHarness` with both settings 0 and the cleared-flag observer bound as `main()` binds it (`outageClears`), `assertNoLeak` over `captured()` after each case: a start-pass launch whose spawn answers it is refused with one onset and arms that persona's timer once at the base wait with the ENVIRONMENT cause, nothing counted, no other call and no `tmux-unresponsive` condition, the other persona untouched (no trigger, timer, notice, flag or call); it arms the same way from calls made outside every attempt (the liveness adapter's `status`, reading `unknown`; a plain `read-pane` through the wrapper; the permission poller's `get`), each raising the outage with one onset and leaving the other persona untouched, and from the JSONL safeguard's `get` it arms every persona once, with one onset each and no attempt; a persona teardown's kill is the exception (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-301; hatch A3): `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` or `ErrConfigMalformed` from it, with the persona applied and with its key no longer applied (4 cases), answers the non-success outcome after one kill, arms nothing and starts no condition, counts nothing, raises the outage with its one onset only for the applied persona, and leaves the other persona untouched; a trigger for a key out of the applied configuration (a plain `read-pane` through the outage wrapper, outside every attempt, answering `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`; the teardown makes no delete, b.jg5 SRJ-715) arms it, and its first retry stops it as not applied with no agent-director call. New features that add significant logic should get their own test file (e.g., `session-manager.test.ts`).

## Isolation (SR-13.2)

Tests never touch the real home or a real install.

- **Temp directories only.** Every file a test reads or writes (config, credentials, state directory, crontable, logs, working directories, agent-director store) sits under the test's own `mkdtempSync` directory, passed explicitly, and removed in `afterEach`.
- **agent-director's settings file.** A test writes `config.toml` only through `writeAgentDirectorConfig` (`tests/test-helpers/ad-settings.ts`) under a temp HOME, never as a hand-written TOML literal and never under the real `~/.agent-director`, and reads it through a reader whose home getter answers that HOME. It takes every settings value (defaults, minimums, key names, the path, refused forms) from `src/ad-settings.ts` or the helper, never typed; the SRD's numbers appear only in the pin table of `tests/ad-settings.test.ts`.
- **Never the real home.** No test reads or writes `~/.claude`, `~/.claude/channels/slack`, `~/.agent-director` or `~/.npm`, and no path in a fixture resolves to them. Code that falls back to `os.homedir()` is tested through `runInFakeHome` (see Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks); code that takes a home or `SLACK_STATE_DIR` gets a temp one. `runPostinstall` falls back to the OS home (and so the real `~/.claude/skills`) when `homeDir` is unset, so `tests/postinstall.test.ts` calls it only through its `postinstall()` wrapper, which refuses options without `homeDir`, with paths from `makeSandbox()` (home, state dir and MCP path under one `mkdtempSync` root).
- **The retired-key record.** A test writes `retired-keys.json` only through `writeRetiredKeysRecord` (`tests/test-helpers/retired-keys.ts`), in its own `mkdtempSync` state directory passed explicitly, never in `~/.claude/channels/slack`; a store under test is loaded over that directory, and a test that reaches `recordStartupError` points its `logDir` (or `SLACK_STATE_DIR`) at the test's own directory.
- **No real server or CLI.** No test calls `main()`, runs `src/server.ts` or `src/cli.ts` as an entry point, or starts a real daemon in-process. The one exception is the usage-text tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` (`unknown subcommand`, and the two `credentials` cases that stop before the script: a usage error and an unknown persona), which run `src/cli.ts` in a child process through the file's `runCli` helper. `runCli` starts Bun by absolute path (`process.execPath`) with its `env` a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call (see `host-safe-env.ts` below): the temp HOME, no tool, so `PATH` is `EMPTY_CHILD_PATH` and names no directory, its own `TMUX_TMPDIR`, and as extras `SLACK_STATE_DIR` and the fixed `BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0`, so Bun writes no transpiler cache under the temp HOME for a tree snapshot to see. Nothing else comes from `process.env`. It has a 15 s time limit and checks that the child spawned and was not killed by it. These cases never reach a subcommand that acts. A new test that spawns the CLI uses `runCli`. The CLI is otherwise tested through `createCli` with injected `CliDeps`; `server.ts` through its importable modules (see Importing server.ts).
- **Inject the `claude_config_dir` check.** The bring-up controller's default `checkConfigDir` resolves an unset `claude_config_dir` against the real OS home's `.claude`, so a dangling real `~/.claude` would hold every persona. Every controller a test builds injects `checkConfigDir`: `checkPersonaConfigDir(persona, { home })` over a scratch home holding a real `.claude` (the `configDirCheckUnder(base)` helpers in `tests/persona-lifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/registry.test.ts`, `tests/health-check.test.ts` and `tests/persona-relaunch-gate.test.ts`; `tests/persona-connections.test.ts`; the reload harness without a real launch), or `checkLaunchConfigDir` where the suite already set the session manager's spawn home (`tests/session-manager.test.ts`, `tests/restart.test.ts`, `tests/persona-bringup.test.ts`, the reload harness with a real launch). `tests/session-manager.test.ts` sets a scratch default spawn home (`_setSpawnHomeDir` over a `default-home` fixture holding a real `.claude`) in `beforeEach`, so no launch resolves against the process home; a test that needs its own replaces it with `useSpawnHome`.
- **CLI log seams.** `openLogAppend`, `closeFd` and `initLogging` are `CliDeps`, so CLI tests inject fakes: no real descriptor is opened and `console` is never taken over. To see which lines reach the log and which the terminal, inject an `initLogging` that swaps `console.error` for a recorder and restore it afterwards. The agent-director calls are built by the exported `createDirectorOps(getClient)`; test it by passing a stub client, not by installing a Client singleton.
- **Fake tokens only.** See the rules under Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks.

### Host safety (b.jg5 SRJ-1301)

Host `bun test` never executes an agent-director binary. The client's discovery (`Client.create()`, `resolveSystemBinary()`) finds the host's real install on `PATH` or at the standard install path under `~/.agent-director`, and a real client opens its store. Redirecting HOME alone moves neither: `PATH` still names the install, and `src/` code that calls `os.homedir()` still sees the launch-time home. So the preload guard first refuses to start under a launch-time home that could reach the operator's real Claude, Slack or agent-director state, and only then redirects the environment.

- **Every client is a stub.** A test that needs an agent-director client gets it from `tests/test-helpers/agent-director-stub.ts`: a `makeStubClient()` installed with `setClientForTests`, or a seam filled with `makeStubCreateClient(...)` (the start gate's `createClient`) or `makeStubResolveSystemBinary(...)`. `makeCloseCountingStubClient(opts?)` gives a `makeStubClient(opts)` stub whose `close()` only counts its calls (`{ client, closes() }`), for a case that checks which client was closed and how often; `makePassingGateDeps(overrides?)` gives the start gate's seams for a run that passes every step (a default `makeStubCreateClient()`, the three API-surface probes passing, an ENOENT state.db stat, UID 1000, a swallowing startup-error recorder and an `exit` that throws), with `overrides` winning over every default. `makeStubClient`'s default `binaryVersion` is `PHASE1_RC_VERSION` (from `tests/test-helpers/agent-director-versions.ts`), which passes CSCB's Phase 1 floor; a test that needs an older or development binary sets `binaryVersion` explicitly, taking the value from that helper. `tests/install-check.test.ts` passes `runInstallCheck` a `makeStubResolveSystemBinary(...)` resolver, and `tests/postinstall.test.ts` passes the probe an injected install check answering canned results; neither mocks `agent-director`.
- **No value import of `Client` or `resolveSystemBinary`.** No test file or test helper holds either as a value from `agent-director`: no named import or re-export (aliased or not), no `export *`, and no read through the module namespace (a property or element read, destructuring, a spread or rest copy, a default or `require` binding, a dynamic `import()`). There is no exception, not even inside `expect(...)`: an identity assertion on `ad.resolveSystemBinary` is a read. Type-only imports (`import type`, an inline `type`) are allowed, and so is spreading the namespace, or a copy of it, into a `mock.module` factory (`{ ...REAL, resolveSystemBinary: stub }`) or comparing a copy with the live namespace entry by entry (see Module Mocks).
- **Every child's `env` is a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call.** Every child-process call in a test file or test helper (the `child_process` functions, `fork` included, however imported; `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.spawnSync` and `$`) passes an options object literal with exactly one `env`, and that `env` is a direct call of `hostSafeChildEnv` imported from `host-safe-env.ts` (see the helper list under Factory Functions). A `Bun.$` template ends in `.env(hostSafeChildEnv(...))`. A child-process function referenced without being called (put in a deps object, re-exported) is refused: the audit can't follow it.
- **The preload guard.** The `[test]` preload of the repository root's `bunfig.toml` and of the `bunfig.toml` in every directory holding a test file (`tests/bunfig.toml`, `tests/integration/bunfig.toml`) loads `tests/test-helpers/host-safety-preload.ts` once, before any test file, when `bun test` starts in one of those directories. Bun reads only the `bunfig.toml` in the directory the run starts in (no upward search) and resolves a relative preload path against that directory, so each file names the guard relative to its own directory, and every entry starts with `./`, `../` or `/` (a bare `a/b.ts` is looked up as a package). The guard is the first `[test]` `preload` entry: Bun loads the entries in order, so an entry before it would run before the refusal. Entries after it are allowed. A new directory of test files gets its own `bunfig.toml` naming the guard the same way. A run started in a directory with no `bunfig.toml` (outside the repository, or one holding no test file, such as `src/`) has no guard. Its first action is the launch-home refusal (next item); a run it accepts goes on. The guard then computes its variables with `preloadRedirectedEnv(process.env, home, tmuxTmpDir)` from `host-safe-env.ts`, which is pure, and applies them to `process.env`: each of `PRELOAD_ENV_NAMES` is set or deleted, nothing else is touched. Its only writes to disk are the new HOME directory and, when the run inherited no valid one, the `TMUX_TMPDIR` directory, both directly under the OS temp directory (`osTempDir()`, the normalized `os.tmpdir()`, so a `TMPDIR` such as `/tmp//` names the same directory as `/tmp`); a refused run makes neither:
  - `HOME`: a new, empty directory directly under the OS temp directory, named with `PRELOAD_HOME_PREFIX`. Every test file shares it; it is never removed, so each run leaves one.
  - `PATH`: the inherited absolute entries, in order, duplicates dropped, without every directory that holds an `agent-director` entry; `EMPTY_CHILD_PATH` when none is left.
  - `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: unset. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names a Claude configuration directory (a run started from a bot's session inherits its persona's), which Claude Code, a hook or any code honouring it would read and write. `TMUX_TMPDIR`: the process's one fenced directory from `childTmuxTmpDir()` (the inherited one when valid, else a new one), the same one `hostSafeChildEnv` hands every child, so a run makes at most one. It is never removed.
  - `SLACK_STATE_DIR`: `<new HOME>/.claude/channels/slack` (not created). It is set rather than unset because the state-directory resolvers fall back to `os.homedir()`.

  It then runs `preloadCheckFailures(process.env)`, the one check shared with `tests/host-safety.test.ts`, and throws, failing the run before any test file loads, when it reports anything. The message names the failed checks by their `PRELOAD_CHECK` labels (a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` still set, empty included, is `claude-config-dir-set`) and HOME, never the environment. No file imports the guard. With the guard in place, a test that forgot its stub fails as not found (`ErrSystemInstallNotFound`, the class label `AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_NOT_FOUND` exported from `src/install-check.ts`) instead of reaching the host's install.
- **The launch-home refusal.** Bun fixes `os.homedir()` and `os.userInfo().homedir` at start-up from the HOME the run was launched with, and the guard cannot move them. So, as its first action, before it makes a directory or changes the environment, the guard checks each launch-time home (`launchTimeHomes()`: both values, duplicates dropped) with `launchHomeRefusal(launchHome, passwdHome(), LIVE_LAUNCH_HOME_PROBE)` from `host-safe-env.ts`. Nothing runs before that check: every module a file loads runs its top-level code before the file's first statement, so the guard loads only `node:` builtins and `./host-safe-env.ts`, and `host-safe-env.ts` only `node:` builtins (no `src/` module, package or other test helper, not even for a type). The decision is pure: its only reads are the probe's (a `LaunchHomeProbe`): `exists` (an `lstat`; a dangling symlink, or an entry that cannot be looked at, counts as present), `canonical` (the path made absolute with every symlink on it followed as far as it exists: the real path of its deepest existing part, a dangling symlink followed to its target, the rest appended, so it names the entry a write to the path would reach) and `tempDir` (`osTempDir()`). Below, a path "resolves" to its `canonical` form. The first rule that applies wins, each with its `LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSAL` label:
  - `launch-home-not-absolute`: the home is empty or a relative path.
  - `launch-home-in-real-home` (passwd home known): the home is the account's passwd home or lies under it, compared by path text first (nothing is probed for a home that matches) and then with both resolved.
  - `launch-home-temp-dir-is-root` (no passwd home): the OS temp directory resolves to the file system root (`/`). Every absolute path lies under the root, so the temp-directory rules would accept any home. Nothing about the home is probed.
  - `launch-home-not-under-temp-dir` (no passwd home): the home does not resolve strictly under the OS temp directory (resolved too); the temp directory itself is refused.
  - `launch-home-holds-slack-state`: anything exists at `<home>/.claude/channels/slack` (`PRELOAD_STATE_DIR_PATH`, the server's default state directory).
  - `launch-home-derived-path-in-real-home` (passwd home known): a path in `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` under the home resolves to the passwd home (as given or resolved) or a path under it. These are the paths `src/` and the agent-director client derive from `homedir()`: `.claude`, `.claude/channels/slack`, `.claude/projects`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/slack-mcp.json`, `.agent-director`, `.agent-director/state.db`, `.agent-director/config.toml` and `.agent-director/bin/agent-director`.
  - `launch-home-derived-path-not-under-temp-dir` (no passwd home): a path in `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` under the home does not resolve strictly under the OS temp directory.
  - `launch-home-holds-agent-director`: the home holds `.agent-director` or an entry at the standard install path.

  `passwdHome()` reads `/etc/passwd` with `passwdHomeFrom`: the first line whose uid field equals the user's uid exactly decides, and a later line for the same uid is never used. There is no passwd home when the file cannot be read, when no line has the uid (as for an account served by LDAP), or when that first line is malformed (fewer than seven fields, or an empty or relative home); `launchHomeRefusal` also takes a relative or empty passwd home as none. With no passwd home the real home is unknown, so the guard fails closed: the temp directory must not resolve to the root, the two temp-directory rules take the real-home rules' places, and the home and every derived path must resolve strictly under the OS temp directory. The root is the only ancestor of a home refused as the temp directory: with no passwd home and the temp directory set to another one (`TMPDIR=/home`, say), a home under it, the real one included, passes the temp-directory rules unless a derived path resolves out of that directory, and is then refused only by `launch-home-holds-slack-state` or `launch-home-holds-agent-director`. On a refusal the guard writes one line to stderr, `launchHomeRefusalMessage(reason, launchHome)`: `host-safety preload: refusing to start: <label> (launch-time home "<path>")` and a pointer to `tests/README.md`, never the environment. It then exits with `LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSED_EXIT_CODE` (78, sysexits' `EX_CONFIG`), so a refusal is told apart from a failing test (exit 1). No test file loads and no directory is made. For a home the guard accepts, no path in `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` resolves into the real home (with no passwd home, each resolves strictly under the OS temp directory, which is not the root), and nothing exists at its Slack state directory or agent-director install paths. When `src/` derives another path from `homedir()`, add it to `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` and to `LINKABLE_DERIVED_PATHS` in `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts`, which writes the list out so that a path dropped from the helper fails its row.
- **HOME under the preload.** The preload moves only what reads the environment (the client's discovery, the `SLACK_STATE_DIR` resolvers). `src/` code that calls `homedir()` directly still answers the launch-time home that the refusal accepted: the start gate's `state.db` path, the state-directory resolvers' fallback with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset, the Claude config-directory default, the default transcript root and `~` expansion. So every run starts with its own scratch HOME outside the real home (`tests/README.md`; `/publish`'s preflight starts its SR-2.3 run the same way), and code that falls back to `os.homedir()` is tested through `runInFakeHome`. Don't patch `os.homedir` in the preload instead: a patched property misses a named import, and a process-wide `mock.module('node:os')` is the top-level mock that Module Mocks forbids.
- **What a test may change.** A test never widens what the guard set: it never sets HOME, `TMUX` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` process-wide and never puts back a `PATH` directory the guard removed. It may narrow `PATH` (a subset of the guard's entries, or a scratch directory of the test's own that holds no `agent-director`) and set `TMUX_TMPDIR` and `SLACK_STATE_DIR`, and restores each to the guard's value in `afterEach`, as `tests/stop-hook-bootstrap.test.ts` (`PATH`, `SLACK_STATE_DIR`) and `tests/host-safety.test.ts` (`PATH`, `TMUX_TMPDIR`) do (see also Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks). One exception: a host-safety refusal test may point `PATH` at a fixture directory of its own that holds a plain, non-executable `agent-director` file, to prove the refusal, and restores `PATH` in `afterEach`. `tests/host-safety.test.ts`'s "a tool's own PATH directory holds an agent-director file" row is the one such case.
- **Enforcement.** `tests/host-safety.test.ts` audits the tree with the TypeScript parser, so text in strings, comments, templates and regex literals never counts: the value-import rule and the child-environment rule over every file `bun test` runs and every test helper; that no file in the repository imports the preload, and that the repository root and every directory holding a test file have a `bunfig.toml` whose first `[test]` preload entry names it with a path entry that resolves to it from that file's directory (a directory with none fails, naming it; an entry before the guard fails, entries after it are allowed); that the preload's first statement after its imports is the launch-home refusal loop over `launchTimeHomes()`, calling `launchHomeRefusal(<home>, passwdHome(), LIVE_LAUNCH_HOME_PROBE)` and, when it gives a reason, ending in `process.exit(LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSED_EXIT_CODE)`, so nothing in the guard runs before the refusal; that the preload loads only `node:` builtins and `./host-safe-env.ts` (`PRELOAD_LOADS`) and `host-safe-env.ts` only `node:` builtins (`HELPER_LOADS`), checked by `guardLoadFindings`, which flags any other static import (side-effect-only and type-only included, so the rule does not depend on what the transpiler drops), `export … from`, `import x = require(…)`, dynamic `import()` or `require()`, and any load whose specifier is not one string literal, because a loaded module's top-level code would run before the refusal; that only the guard's own files (`REAL_HOME_FILES`: `host-safe-env.ts`, the preload, `tests/host-safety.test.ts` and `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts`) reference `realHome` or `passwdHome`, the helpers that answer the real home's path; and, over `src/` and `scripts/`, the SRJ-121 call sites (`Client.create` only in the startup gate's module, `resolveSystemBinary` as a value only in the server, the install check and `/publish`'s check). It then runs the shared `preloadCheckFailures` on the live environment (every name in `PRELOAD_ENV_NAMES`) and, only when that reports nothing, calls `runStartupGate()` and `runInstallCheck()` un-injected: both must fail as not found. `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts` covers the launch-home refusal: `passwdHomeFrom` over passwd texts; every rule and their order over a recording fake probe, with the passwd home known and unknown, a temp directory resolving to the root, the `/home` temp directory that lets the would-be real home through, and one row per derived path; the live probe over fixtures beside a fake real home, and against the OS temp directory with no passwd home; the guard in a `bun test` child started from each directory with a `bunfig.toml` (the repository root, `tests/` and `tests/integration/`), refused under a fake home holding `.claude/channels/slack` and accepted under an empty one; that this run's `homedir()`-derived defaults resolve outside the passwd home (with no passwd entry, strictly under the OS temp directory); and preflight's SR-2.3 scratch HOME. A refusal test launches its child only with a fake home under its own `mkdtempSync` root, never with the real home.
- **Fixing a finding.** Inject the stub, or pass `env: hostSafeChildEnv(...)` directly in the call. When the preload check fails, run `bun test` from a directory whose `bunfig.toml` loads the guard (the repository root, `tests/` or `tests/integration/`), so the guard loads and sets HOME and `PATH` itself; still start with a scratch HOME (`tests/README.md`). When the bunfig audit names a directory, give it a `bunfig.toml` whose first `[test]` preload entry names the guard relative to it. When the load audit flags the guard or `host-safe-env.ts`, write what the guard needs in `host-safe-env.ts` from `node:` builtins instead of importing it. When the guard refuses to start (exit 78, `host-safety preload: refusing to start: <label>`), relaunch with a new, empty scratch HOME outside the real home, made under a `TMPDIR` outside it too (and not `/`), as `tests/README.md` shows. Never loosen an audit or a refusal rule, add an exemption or widen what the preload set to make room.

### Integration scripts run only in docker CI

The integration scripts (`tests/integration/*.sh`), their shared helper (`tests/integration/lib/scenario.sh`), their fixtures (`tests/integration/fixtures/`: the Test 4 and Test 11 drivers, `stub-claude.sh` and the Slack stub server) and `tests/runner.sh` install the packed package, write a persona config, start the server and spawn bots. They run only inside the `cscb-ci` docker container, started by the `ci` skill (`/ci`), which runs `tests/runner.sh` and reports `PASS` or `FAIL`.

- Never run them on a dev box or on any host without container support, and never against the real home. If docker is not available, report the integration run as not done; don't run the scripts directly.
- Their config and credentials files are written inside the container; the scripts never read a config from the host.
- `bun test` does not run them. `tests/integration/session-leader.test.ts` is the one `bun test` file under `tests/integration/`: it spawns only a throwaway child and touches no CSCB state. The Slack stub server has no `bun test` suite of its own: Test 10 exercises it end to end.
- `tests/README.md` has the suite's layout, the runner's discovery order (Tests 1 to 4, then every other `test-*.sh` in version order), the helper's contract and how to add a scenario. A new scenario sources the helper, which gives it its own scratch state dir, port and persona-name tag, bounded polling waits and a cleanup trap.
- `CSCB_SLACK_API_URL` (the Slack API base URL override, honoured only for an `http://127.0.0.1…` or `http://[::1]…` URL) exists for the scenarios alone. Test 10 sets it to point a live start at the Slack stub. A unit test passes an env object to `resolveSlackApiUrlOverride`, or a `slackApiUrl` to the connection manager or the option builders. The one case that sets it in `process.env`, to prove it is not read from there, restores it in `finally`.

### The /ci-live runner

The `/ci-live` runner (`ci-live/`, see `docker/README.md`) has its own dependency, `playwright-core`, installed only in `ci-live/node_modules`. Its unit tests live in `tests/` like every other suite.

- Import only from `ci-live/lib/`, `ci-live/provision/`, `ci-live/checks/` and `ci-live/dry-run/`. Never import `ci-live/run.ts`, `ci-live/main.ts`, `ci-live/maintenance.ts`, `ci-live/runtime/` or `ci-live/browser/` (`driver.ts` and the flows): they load `playwright-core`, directly or through `main.ts` or `ci-live/runtime/workspace.ts`, so `bun test` and `bun run typecheck` would fail on a clone where the runner's dependency is not installed. Put logic a test must reach in `ci-live/lib/` or `ci-live/provision/`, as the memory watchdog (`lib/memory-watchdog.ts`), the copy of the container's own logs (`lib/container-logs.ts`), the stray-app rules (`provision/app-listing.ts`) and the prompt guard (`checks/prompt-guard.ts`, driven through `PromptGuardDeps` with a fake trail and the shared fake clock) are.
- Put no `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` file under `ci-live/`: `bun test` would pick it up.
- Drive I/O through the runner's seams (`SecureFs` for the secret store, `ScanFs` for the secrecy scan, `LockDeps` for the run lock's file access and PID liveness test and a collecting warning sink for its stale-lock `WARNING`, the spawn function for docker and the host probes, the injected fetch and clock; `ContainerLogsSink` for the copy of the container's logs (an in-memory sink, or `containerLogsSink` over a `mkdtempSync` results dir) with a fake `ContainerExec` for the container and the shared fake clock as the collector's `clock` (`CollectorClock`), which a caller's wait runs on; for the memory watchdog, its `WatchdogSources` and `WatchdogClock`, the file reader `readHostCgroup` takes and the `/proc` reader, `ProcReader`). A test never reads `~/.config/cscb-test/` or the host's cgroup files, takes the real run lock, starts a container or reaches Slack.
- The code no test may import (`ci-live/run.ts`, `ci-live/main.ts`, `ci-live/maintenance.ts`, `ci-live/runtime/`, `ci-live/browser/`) is pinned by the source audit in `tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts`: its environment reads, spawn sites, host commands (the HOST check's two read-only probes the only host-side agent-director and tmux argv), the staged agent-director binary (selected only through `selectAgentDirectorBinary`, copied into a fresh temp dir removed in a `finally`, never in a spawn or docker argv), the tmux and agent-director commands inside its `bash -c` scripts (collected by `shellScriptCommands`, with a script it cannot read on a closed list of one), docker subcommands (the exact `docker stats` and `docker stop` argv included), leftover removal, the run lock's acquires and their warning sinks, signal handling (`main.ts`'s `stopRun` and `maintenance.ts`'s stop), the memory watchdog's wiring, the cleanup order, the copy of the container's own logs awaited before every removal or stop of the container (so a failed check can still be traced once the container is gone) and sealed before the closing scan, `appsCommand`'s order, the prompt guard's wiring and the browser's bounds in `browser/driver.ts` (`ensureSignedIn`'s idle and the one-at-a-time flows included). A change there that adds a host command, a `bash -c` tmux or agent-director command, a spawn site, a lock acquire, an environment read or a removal or stop of the container, or reorders a pinned sequence, fails the audit; widen or update the audit for that one item in the same change, and never loosen a pattern to get it green.
- The runner's tokens are fakes built at runtime, as everywhere under `tests/` (see Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks); `tests/secrecy-audit.test.ts` rejects a token literal.

## Fixture Patterns

### Factory Functions

Every test file defines factory functions that create fixtures with sensible defaults and optional overrides:

```
makePersonaConfig(overrides?, baseDir?) — a resolved PersonaConfig with one default persona
makeMultiPersonaConfig(specs, baseDir, overrides?) — a resolved PersonaConfig with one persona per spec
makeTransport() — minimal transport stub
makeServer() — minimal MCP server stub
```

Always use factory functions instead of hardcoding fixture values in individual tests. When a new field is added to a type, update the factory function — all tests automatically pick up the default.

Reload-controller tests build their configuration directory, personas and runs with `makeReloadHarness` (see Reload Tests), not by hand.

Persona-loader tests, and tests of persona-keyed code such as `spawnForPersona`, `startupSessionManager` and `launchSession` in `src/session-manager.ts`, use the shared persona-config helper, `tests/test-helpers/persona-config.ts`. It is the only config fixture; a route-keyed config appears only as raw JSON in a pre-persona rejection case. The CLI's `loadConfig` dependency returns a resolved `PersonaConfig`, so CLI tests build it with these helpers too. The persona-config helper provides:

```
makePersona(overrides?, baseDir?) — one PersonaInput entry in file form; default paths sit under baseDir
makePersonaConfigInput(overrides?, baseDir?) — a PersonaConfigInput file-form config with one default persona
makePersonaConfig(overrides?, baseDir?) — a resolved PersonaConfig, as loadPersonaConfig returns it, except mcp_config_path (see below)
makeMultiPersonaConfig(specs, baseDir, overrides?) — a resolved PersonaConfig with one persona per PersonaSpec, in order
makeStandInPersonaConfig(personas, baseDir, overrides?) — makeMultiPersonaConfig for stand-in personas keyed and named by one channel ID each
writeConfigFile(dir, input) — writes input as JSON to <dir>/config.json and returns the path
```

Use `makeMultiPersonaConfig` when a test needs several personas. Each `PersonaSpec` is any resolved `Persona` field except `index`; `overrides` sets the server-wide fields as for `makePersonaConfig`.

- It runs no validation, so a stand-in persona can set `key` to a channel ID directly.
- Each persona defaults to its own `all` channel, with prompts to that channel and DMs off. A spec with no channels gets `permission_prompts: 'dm'` but DMs still off, a pair the loader rejects; set `dm` in that spec yourself.
- It throws when two personas share a name or a key.
- `baseDir` is required; pass the test's `mkdtempSync` directory.

`makeStandInPersonaConfig` is kept for older suites whose fixtures key personas by channel ID; new tests use `makeMultiPersonaConfig` with real persona names. Each record key is a channel ID that becomes the persona's `name` and `key`, its one `all` channel and its `permission_prompts` target; the record value sets further fields such as `working_directory`. Personas keep record order, and everything else, including the required `baseDir`, is as for `makeMultiPersonaConfig`.

For the other helpers, `baseDir` defaults to the OS temp directory; pass the test's own `mkdtempSync` directory when paths must exist or be unique to the test. `writeConfigFile` writes only into the caller-supplied temp directory and has no default location. Pass `loadPersonaConfig` a temp home as well, so `~` never expands to the real home. Remove both the temp directory and the temp home in `afterEach`.

Build agent-director rows in tests with the canned-row helpers in `tests/test-helpers/agent-director-stub.ts` (`cannedListRow`, `cannedGetResult`, `cannedGetResultPlural`), never by hand. Every row they build is persona-labelled (b.av2 SR-13.4):

- **Default form** — `cannedListRow({ claude_instance_id })`: the row stands for the persona whose key is the instance ID without its `cscb_` prefix. Labels are exactly `service=cscb` and `persona=<key>` (no `config_dir`, no `channel`), tmux `slack_bot_<key>`, and `cwd` is `defaultCannedRowCwd()`, the working directory of the default persona fixture (`makePersona()`, `<tmpdir>/personas/test_bot/work`; nothing creates it). The stub client's default `get` row uses this form. Use it for permission-poller and click-handler rows, and pair it with a `getPersona` stub that knows that key.
- **Persona form** — `cannedListRow(overrides, persona, home)`, likewise `cannedGetResult` and `cannedGetResultPlural`.

A `channel` label appears only in explicit negative rows that test the rejection of pre-persona rows (the poller skipping a row with no `persona` label, the start sweep killing a live one and keeping it): override `labels` to carry only the old `channel` label.

For the persona form, pass a resolved persona (e.g. from `makePersonaConfig`). The row then carries what a spawn of that persona writes: `cwd` = its working directory, `cscb_<key>`, `slack_bot_<key>`, and the `service`, `persona` and `config_dir` labels. The collision ladder and the start sweep replace a row whose `cwd` or `config_dir` label doesn't match (b.av2 SR-6.2 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1503 and SRJ-1504, SR-6.3: the ladder with no row deleted, a finished row by a reuse spawn of the same id and a live row through the live-row sequence first), so a fixture meant to reach a resume, reconnect or wait path must use this form. `home` is required and the persona form throws without it; there is no OS-home fallback. The `config_dir` label must be computed under the same home the session manager's `_setSpawnHomeDir` seam uses, or it won't match the one the code computes, so pass that home. To test a guard, override `cwd` or `labels` explicitly. `spawnForPersona` joins a launch already in flight for the same key, so a suite that can leave a launch unsettled calls `_resetInFlightLaunches()` in `afterEach`.

To test that only one launch per persona is in flight, wrap the stub with `holdSpawns(stub, shouldHold?)` from the same file. Each `spawn` whose instance ID passes `shouldHold` (all by default) stays open until the test settles it; other spawns go to the stub's original `spawn`. The handle exposes `calls` (every spawn received), `held()` (instance IDs still open), `entered(id)` (resolves once a spawn for `id` is issued), `release(id)` and `fail(id, err)` (settle the oldest held spawn for `id`), and `releaseAll()` for teardown.

To keep a live-row sequence's `find-missing` run outstanding while a case drives other work (the start pass, an apply, a stop, a lost message; b.jg5 SRJ-706), wrap the stub with `holdFindMissing(stub)` from the same file (`FindMissingHold`). Every `find-missing` call stays open until the test settles it, oldest first: the handle exposes `calls` (every call received since the hold, in order; held calls are not in the stub's own call log), `heldCount()`, `entered(count?)` (resolves once that many calls, 1 by default, have been received), `release(result)` (resolve the oldest with a placement built with `cannedFindMissing`), `fail(err)` (reject the oldest) and `releaseAll()` (resolve every held call with the empty result) for cleanup.

To assert which agent-director calls a case made (for example, none for a persona that is not up), use the shared stub call-log helper in the same file rather than a hand-rolled recorder, so every suite reads the stub's calls the same way.

To stand in for `resolveSystemBinary` (the start gate's system-install lookup, the runtime version re-check's resolve, `/publish`'s SR-2.5 check), use `makeStubResolveSystemBinary(opts?)` from the same file; no test runs a binary to learn a version. It returns an `(opts?) => Promise<{ path, version }>` function. With no options every call resolves with `PHASE1_RC_VERSION`, which passes CSCB's Phase 1 floor, at `/usr/local/bin/agent-director`; `path` changes that path, `version` the version of every call, and `throws` rejects every call with that error. `outcomes` answers the calls in order, one entry per call, and once the list runs out its last entry answers every later call: `{ version, path? }` resolves with that version (at `path`, else the builder's `path`), `{ throws }` rejects with that error, and `{ never: true }` returns a promise that never settles, for a time-limit case. `outcomes` given with `throws` or `version`, or empty, throws when the stub is built. `calls` records each call's argument, a call that never settles included.

**agent-director errors.** Build an agent-director error in a test with the stub's builder wherever one exists. The three errors only the Phase 1 client declares (`ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`) are built only with their builders, never from a class. For an error the stub has no builder for, a test may use `new` on the 0.10.0 client's own class. A test of a site's error handling builds the error with the stub builders and imports the class it expects from `src/ad-error-class.ts` (`AD_ERROR_CLASS_*`), never a literal label. Assert a call-capture array with `toHaveLength`: Bun's `toEqual([])` also passes on `[undefined]`.

Each builder uses the 0.10.0 client's own class, except:

- `errGeneric(verb, errName, message?)`, which builds the base `AgentDirectorError` for any `errName`; a name CSCB gives no handling is UNCLASSIFIED, a refusal at every launch site (b.jg5 SRJ-313), so a case that wants a launch failure uses `errTmuxSessionCreate` (or `errGeneric` with that name), never an invented name;
- `errAmbiguousRequest()` and `errPermissionRequestNotFound()`, which build the base `AgentDirectorError` with the error's `errName` although 0.10.0 exports a class for each, because the code under test recognises both by `errName`;
- the builders for the three Phase-1-only errors.

Until the Phase 1 client is adopted (b.jg5 E37), those Phase-1-only builders return the 0.10.0 client's `AgentDirectorError` carrying the error's name (as both `name` and `errName`, from the `ERR_TMUX_*_NAME` strings in `src/agent-director-errors.ts`), its verb and its description, so they classify by name. No test imports a Phase-1-only class, in a named import or a re-export.

The description words CSCB matches come from `src/ad-description-phrases.ts`, and the builders take them from there. A test that checks for one imports the constant from that module, never a literal. The builders' default names are the default persona fixture's: `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_NAME`, `STUB_INSTANCE_ID`, and `STUB_TMUX_SOCKET_PATH` for the socket.

- **`ErrTmuxUnresponsive` (by name)**: `errTmuxUnresponsive(verb?, description?)` (verb `resume`; `status` only reads the store and never returns it; by default a tmux call that did not answer and did nothing). The variants CSCB tells apart: `errTmuxUnresponsiveLaunchTimeout(verb?, instanceId?)` (verb `spawn`, or `resume`; carries `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`), `errTmuxUnresponsiveStillStopping(verb?, sessionName?)` and `errTmuxUnresponsiveStillStarting(verb?, sessionName?)` (verb `resume`, session `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_NAME`; the description names the quoted session name, as agent-director's does, and carries `STILL_STOPPING_PHRASE` or `STILL_STARTING_PHRASE`), `errTmuxUnresponsiveAfterDuplicateSession(verb?)` (verb `resume`; tmux answered "duplicate session" and the session holding the name could not be read, so nothing was started), and `errTmuxUnresponsiveNewRowEnded(verb?, sessionName?)` (verb `spawn`, session `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_NAME`; HO rev 26, b.jg5 SRJ-111: a plain spawn's `tmux new-session` answered "duplicate session" and its re-lookup of the holder did not answer, so agent-director ended the new row; the description names the quoted session and carries `NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE` and the retry `NEW_ROW_ENDED_RETRY`, the stub's own export, "retry with reuse_finished once the session name is free", since `src/` keys nothing on it and holds no constant for it; it carries none of `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`, `STILL_STOPPING_PHRASE` or `STILL_STARTING_PHRASE`, so it is no launch timeout).
- **`ErrTmuxKillFailed` (by name)**: `errTmuxKillFailed(sessionName?, description?, pids?)`, verb `kill`. `description` is a `KillFailedDescription`: `'outlived-exit-wait'` (the default; a kill was sent and the agent process outlived the exit wait), `'pane-process-survived'` (a kill was sent and another process of the labelled session's panes outlived it), `'unverifiable-session-present'` (a kill was sent, the process cannot be checked and the labelled session is still there) or `'no-session-no-kill'` (no session or pane of this launch while the process runs; "no kill was sent"). Every description carries the quoted session name, "retry kill later" and "never delete this row" (`RETRY_KILL_LATER_PHRASE`, `NEVER_DELETE_ROW_PHRASE`). Only `'pane-process-survived'` names a pid: each of `pids` as `pid <n>`, joined with ", " (default `STUB_SURVIVOR_PIDS`, one fake pid above Linux's largest), the form `SURVIVOR_PID_PATTERN` matches and `survivorPids` lists in order; the other three ignore `pids` and name none. The builder checks its own text with `survivorPids` and throws if the pids it names are not exactly those given, or if `'pane-process-survived'` is given no pid. `KILL_FAILED_DESCRIPTIONS` lists all four for `test.each`.
- **`ErrTmuxSessionConflict` (by name)**: `errTmuxSessionConflict(verb, conflictCase, sessionName?, options?)`. `conflictCase` is a `ConflictCase`, one per case of ADSRD SR-1.4: `no-valid-id`, `different-id`, `another-store`, `own-id`, `leftover`, `scan-leftover` (the pre-spawn scan's refusal: "left over from an earlier life", the session's tmux id `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_ID`, "nothing was written and no row was created"), `duplicate-session-leftover` (a plain spawn at "duplicate session": "its label names this instance id", "left over from an earlier life", "the new row was ended"), `not-this-launch`, `pane-not-found` (also "this row's own id"), `conflicting-labels`, `never-reported-in` (also "this row's own id" and "no kill was sent"), and `unrecognised`, which carries none of the case words. `not-this-launch` from `kill` also carries "this row's own id" and "no kill was sent". `CONFLICT_CASES` lists all twelve. Every description carries the `agent-director list --tmux-session-name <quoted name>` line. `different-id` and `another-store` ("another agent-director store") say the session is another row's (another store's) agent and must not be ended, and point to no "Operator actions"; every other description points a human to "Operator actions". `options` is a `ConflictOptions` selecting the variants the positional form cannot: `plainSpawn` on `different-id` or `another-store` (a plain spawn at "duplicate session": also "its label does not name this instance id" and "the new row was ended"), `notAdopted` on `pane-not-found` (a lost create reply: also "the agent's pane was not adopted"), `scan` on `conflicting-labels` (the pre-spawn scan found an agent-director label value set at the server, global or global-window scope: also "nothing was written and no row was created"); an option set on any other case throws. No description names a command that ends a session; "no kill was sent" is the one mention of a kill. The case words and extras come from `src/ad-description-phrases.ts`. A test that iterates the latch's conflict cases uses `CONFLICT_CASE_ROWS` from `conflict-cases.ts` (under Other shared fixture builders), which covers every entry of `CONFLICT_CASES`.
- **0.10.0 classes**: `errTmuxNotAvailable(socketPath?, verb?)` (verb `spawn`; with `socketPath` that socket is not accessible to this user, without it tmux could not be run); `errTmuxNotAvailableDifferentServer(socketPath?, verb?)` (verb `resume`, socket `STUB_TMUX_SOCKET_PATH`; other single-row verbs that call tmux, such as `read-pane`, also return it, `status` never; carries `DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE`); `errTmuxNotAvailableNewRowEnded(verb?, sessionName?)` (verb `spawn`; the ENVIRONMENT form of `errTmuxUnresponsiveNewRowEnded`: tmux could not be run for the re-lookup, with the same words, `NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE` and `NEW_ROW_ENDED_RETRY`, HO rev 26); `errTmuxCaptureFailed(sessionName?, verb?)` (verb `read-pane`; the session is gone); `errSpawnNotPausable(verb?)` (verb `pause`); `errSystemInstallDisappeared(verb?, binaryPath?)` (verb `status`, path `STUB_RESOLVE_DEFAULT_PATH`). Beside `errSpawnNotInteractive(verb?)`, `errSpawnNotInteractiveLeftover(sessionName?, verb?)` (the session is a leftover of an earlier launch) and `errSpawnNotInteractiveNoLaunchStart(verb?)` (a `pending` row with no launch start), both verb `send-keys`. `errSendKeysWhileRelayed()` builds the client's `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` (verb `send-keys`: agent-director refuses keys to a row that sits on a relayed permission prompt, and nothing was sent), which classes UNCLASSIFIED (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-118); use it rather than `errGeneric` with that name. `errInvalidFlags(verb?)` builds the client's `ErrInvalidFlags` (verb `decide`; pass `spawn` or `resume` for a launch verb's refusal). `errCwdNotFound(verb?, cwd?)` and `errCwdNotADirectory(verb?, cwd?)` (verb `spawn`, `cwd` `/x`) build the client's directory errors, and `errTmuxSessionCreateStaysPending(verb?)` (verb `spawn`) an `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` whose description ends with agent-director's sentence that the row could not be restored and stays pending (`RESTORE_SENTENCE_STAYS_PENDING`), built through `withRestoreSentence`. `RESTORE_SENTENCES` holds HO rev 28's four restore sentences that can end a failed `resume`'s or reuse's description (restored to its prior state; changed after the move and left as it is; removed after the move, so nothing restored; could not be restored and stays pending), and `withRestoreSentence(err, sentence)` gives `err` again, same class, verb and name, its description ending with `sentence`, so it classifies as `err` does. CSCB matches no part of any of them (the retry's read of the row decides), and a case's row stays as the case scripts it, never derived from the sentence.
- **No class in any client**: an unknown name arrives as `ErrUnknownErrorName`, built as the client builds it: `unknownName` is the name and `envelope` is the binary's `{ err_name, err_description }`. The client's own `verb` and `errDescription` stay as it sets them, so read the binary's description from `envelope.err_description`. `errUnknownErrorName(unknownName?, description?)` builds any name (default `ErrFromALaterBinary`); `errInternal(description?)` an `ErrInternal`; `errSchemaMismatch(description?)` an `ErrSchemaMismatch` (by default the store could not be opened), while the other two store-open names, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired` and `ErrStoreOpen`, are built with `errUnknownErrorName` and the `ERR_*_NAME` constants from `src/agent-director-errors.ts`; `errUnusableName(fault?)` the unusable-recorded-name `ErrInternal`, carrying `UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE`, where `fault` is an `UnusableNameFault` (`'empty'`, the default, `'control-character'` or `'stored-differently'`, all in `UNUSABLE_NAME_FAULTS`; `tests/ad-error-class.test.ts` and `tests/conflict-latch.test.ts` iterate `UNUSABLE_NAME_FAULTS` directly, and the session-manager, server, restart and health-check cases take their UNUSABLE NAME answers from `UNUSABLE_NAME_CASE_ROWS` in `conflict-cases.ts`, which crosses it with every site kind); `errConfigMalformed(key?, value?, minimum?, unit?)` an `ErrConfigMalformed` in agent-director's refusal form, `config <path>: refused [tmux] values: [tmux] <key> = <value>, below its safe minimum <minimum> <unit>. A missing key, or 0, gives the default.` (default `starting_session_seconds` = `30` below `60` `s`; `unit` is `s` or `ms`).
- **Every UNAVAILABLE form**: `UNAVAILABLE_FORMS` is the one table of UNAVAILABLE forms (b.jg5 SRJ-104), each an `UnavailableForm` tuple `[label, make(verb), causeKind]`: `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` and its three variants (`ErrTmuxUnresponsive, still stopping`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive, still starting`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive, launch timeout`), `ErrCallTimeout`, `ErrUnknownErrorName`, `a wrapped UnknownError` (CSCB's `UnknownError` wrapper), `ErrTmuxKillFailed` (cause `kill-failed`; only a kill answers it) and `a plain Error`, every other form with cause `unavailable`. A file takes its subset with `unavailableForms(...picks)`, in the order given: a label picks its row as is, a `[label, as]` pair relabels it, and a label the table lacks throws. Never write a file-local copy of the table.

**Dead-session causes, escalate-dead verdicts and dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-611).** Tests import the causes (`DEAD_SESSION_CAUSE_*`), the verdicts (`ESCALATE_DEAD_WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`, `ESCALATE_DEAD_ROW_ABSENT_AT_PANE_READ`), the evidence texts (`ESCALATE_DEAD_EVIDENCE`) and the evidence helpers (`isDeadEvidence`, `carriedDeadEvidenceOf`, `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`, `DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`, `describeDeadEvidence`) from `src/session-manager.ts`, and iterate the exported lists `DEAD_SESSION_CAUSES` and `ESCALATE_DEAD_VERDICTS` rather than a copy of their values, so a new cause or verdict is covered by every case that walks them. The expected answer of each is `DEAD_EVIDENCE_OF` (`tests/test-helpers/dead-evidence.ts`), the one table of which cause or verdict is dead evidence: keyed by `DeadEvidenceSource`, so a new value fails the typecheck until it has an answer there, and written out by hand, never asked of the code under test. `tests/session-manager.test.ts`'s SRJ-611 describe alone checks `isDeadEvidence` against it; other suites (`tests/restart.test.ts`) read it for what a cause or verdict leads to and never re-assert `isDeadEvidence`. Expected lines come from their builders (`deadSessionRouteLine`, `deadEvidenceVoidedLine` with `deadEvidenceVoidingRead` or a `DEAD_EVIDENCE_VOIDED_BY_*` text, `waitRowFinishedLine`, `waitRowAbsentLine`, `promptRowSweepFinishedLine`, `joinedLaunchDropsDeadEvidenceLine`, `relaunchWithoutKillLine` with its reason, `killVoidsVerdictLine`), each pinned once as a literal. A cause's GONE-ness (`DEAD_EVIDENCE_OF`) never changes with the path; whether it leads to a kill or a sequence also depends on the path's last read, since dead evidence covers one life: a read of the row as `ended`, `missing` or gone voids every piece the path holds, and a reconnect's `row-not-interactive` voids a carried verdict. So a session-manager case states, in its hand-written row, whether the path still holds live evidence at the not-resumable step (`liveEvidence`) and which pieces it voided, in line order (`voided`); a restart case crosses each verdict with each `dead` re-probe, and expects no kill after a first probe or re-probe that read a row: only an `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reading, which reads no row, keeps the kill (and, after a GONE-based verdict, the verdict). A case whose subject is the restart kill reaches it through that reading: `installGoneRestartProbe` (`tests/test-helpers/recovery-harness.ts`) where the kill's outcome is the subject, or a real install-gone `status` read through the stub, with its read-error cause and `ad-unreachable` onset asserted, where the case means the production path. A restart-path escalate-dead answer is built as the adapter builds it, `{ outcome: 'escalate-dead', deadEvidence: carriedDeadEvidenceOf(verdict) }` (`ReconnectEscalateDead`). Build every carried value through `carriedDeadEvidenceOf` (or `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`): `CarriedDeadEvidence` carries a type-only brand, so an object literal fails the typecheck. The one exception is the `handBuilt` helper in `tests/session-manager.test.ts`, which casts past the brand to pin the builders' run-time shape and to hand the code a deliberately inconsistent value (an `evidence` flag its source does not prove); never copy it into another file.

**Phase 1 results.** The Phase 1 result fields `kill_sent`, `launch_started_at` and `pre_trust` are typed by `src/ad-phase1-types.ts`, which also names the `liveness_note` values CSCB tells apart (`LivenessNote`); tests take those types from there, never from `agent-director`. A Phase 1 field given as `undefined`, or left out, is absent from the built result, as from a binary older than Phase 1, with one exception: a `pending` row's launch start (below).

- `cannedKillResult(killSent?)`: `{ kill_sent }`, or `{}` without an argument. The stub's default `kill` result is `{}`.
- `cannedStatusResult(overrides?)`: `{ state: 'waiting' }` by default, which is also the stub client's default `status` answer (`cannedStatusResult()`). Its one Phase 1 override is `launch_started_at`: agent-director's `status` result has no `liveness_note`.
- `cannedGetResult` and `cannedListRow` take `launch_started_at` and `liveness_note` as overrides. A `pending` row from any of the three canned builders (`cannedStatusResult`, `cannedGetResult`, `cannedListRow`, and so the stub client's default answers) shows the sample launch start `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_DEFAULT` (`SAMPLE_LAUNCH_STARTS.fractional`) unless the overrides have a `launch_started_at` key, since a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start latches the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-513). "No launch start" is an explicit request: `launch_started_at: SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_NONE` (`undefined`: the key is left out of the row) or `launch_started_at: null` (the key shown as `null`). A row in any other state has no launch start, and no row has a note, unless given one; an explicit override wins in every state. Launch starts: `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_FRACTIONAL`, `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_WHOLE` and `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_NONE` (`undefined`), all three by form in `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_STARTS` for `test.each`; take launch starts from these constants and never type a timestamp. Notes: `provenanceNote` (`provenance_conflict`, the only note that latches a persona, with the CONFLICT case "conflicting labels"; the stub's own spelling of the wire value, not `src/`'s constant, so a misspelt constant fails a test), `nonLatchingNotes` (every other note agent-director names: `tmux_server_changed`, `process_not_seen_session_present`, `process_not_seen_tmux_unchecked`, `probe_eacces`, `tmux_session_name_empty`, `tmux_session_name_control_char`, `tmux_session_name_rewritten`, typed as the 0.10.0 client's free text) and `unknownNote` (a note CSCB does not know, `provenance_conflict_cleared`, so a prefix match of the latching note fails). Take note values from here, never type them; the note-rule cases in `tests/session-manager.test.ts` and `tests/conflict-latch.test.ts` iterate `nonLatchingNotes` and `unknownNote`: every entry at the pure decision, the collision `get` and the post-run `get`s, and a sample of them (one or two listed notes, `unknownNote` and no note) at the other sites, which share the one note rule.
- `cannedSpawnResult(claudeInstanceId?, preTrust?)` and `cannedResumeResult(claudeInstanceId?, preTrust?)`: `preTrust` sets `pre_trust` (`ok`, `skipped` or `failed`); leave it out for a result from a binary older than Phase 1, which carries no `pre_trust` key.
- `PRE_TRUST_VALUES`: the three `pre_trust` values (`readonly PreTrust[]`), for `test.each` with the two builders above; an absent field is their `preTrust` left out. It is built from a private record keyed and valued by every `PreTrust` member, so a member missing from it, an extra key or a misspelt one fails `bun run typecheck`. Tests take `pre_trust` values from this list and never type them.
- A recorded `spawn` may be a reuse spawn (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-708): `spawnCalls` and `holdSpawns`' `calls` are typed `Phase1SpawnParams` (`src/ad-phase1-types.ts`), so a test reads `reuse_finished` with no cast; the stub answers a reuse like any spawn, from the same queue and knobs.
- `cannedFindMissing({ rows })`: `rows` maps each row ID to where a sweep reports it, `'ids'`, `'unverified_ids'` or `'neither'` (`FindMissingRowPlacement`; `'neither'` on a row read `pending` models a row the run did not judge); both ID lists are sorted and `count` and `unverified` are their lengths. `cannedFindMissing(overrides?)` builds the result field by field (empty by default).

**Stub client knobs.** A `<verb>Queue` on `makeStubClient` holds `cannedOk(value)` and `cannedErr(error)` entries; N entries answer the next N calls in order.
